text_run.content: External migration simplifies the process of moving your vector databases and search systems to Zilliz Cloud. Whether you're migrating from vector databases like Pinecone and Qdrant, or from search engines with vector capabilities like Elasticsearch and OpenSearch, Zilliz Cloud provides migration tools to ensure data integrity while minimizing migration complexity.
Zilliz Cloud supports migration from leading vector databases and search platforms:
Dense vector support with full-text search
Our migration tools provide extensive configuration options to ensure your data structure fits perfectly on Zilliz Cloud:
Rename fields during migration to match your preferred naming style
Convert flexible metadata into fixed, structured fields for better performance.
If your metadata includes text, converting it to a fixed field will create a
field. This enables Full Text Search on that text. For details, refer to
Add new fields beyond source data to accommodate evolving requirements
Zilliz Cloud detects and maps field types automatically, with option to adjust manually

By default, Zilliz Cloud retains the source table name for the target collection; if a duplicate name is detected, the system issues an error alert so the user can rename it. For naming‐rule conflicts, such as when a source table name contains a hyphen (
), Zilliz Cloud will either automatically convert the hyphen (
) or raise an error prompting the user to adjust, depending on the data source
Set up data distribution to match how you plan to query your data
Organize data using either automatic partitioning or custom groupings
Create, keep, or modify unique identifiers for your records
Set whether fields can contain null values and define default values
Choose to fail immediately on errors or skip up to 1,000 problematic rows to continue migration

The migration follows a three-phase approach designed to ensure data integrity and provide visibility throughout the process:
: Provide authentication credentials (API keys, connection strings) to access your source system and test connection
: Choose specific indexes, collections, or tables to migrate
: Select your Zilliz Cloud cluster and database as the destination
This phase involves two key components:
: The system identifies vector fields, scalar fields, and metadata
: Adjust field names and types as needed
: Review and confirm data type mappings between source and target
: Configure shards, partition keys, and nullable fields based on your requirements
For optimal performance, configure shards based on your data volume:
Configure how the migration job handles error rows:
(default): Migration halts immediately when any row fails - best for critical data requiring 100% accuracy
: Continue migration while skipping problematic rows - suitable for large datasets where some data quality issues are acceptable
Once configuration is complete, execute the migration and track progress:
: Track migration status through the Jobs page
: View rows migrated, error counts, and estimated completion time
: Review detailed code logs if issues occur
: Automatic row count verification ensures data completeness
Before starting your migration, be aware of these common limitations that apply across all supported data sources:
Manually create indexes and load the collections post-migration. For detailed steps, refer to
Ensure source contains data before migrating
Verify your source has vector fields before migration
Some specialized data types may not transfer
Review platform-specific guides for data type mappings
